\chapter{Optima Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{optima_algorithms:optima-algorithms}}\label{\detokenize{optima_algorithms::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Optima}} is the constrained optimization layer built in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussMa}} on top of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} and autodiff runtime from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussQit}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This split is intentional:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussQit}} owns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, autodiff transforms, and backend compute

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussMa}} owns numerical optimization logic and solver policy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{optima(...)}} is the public constrained\sphinxhyphen{}solver entry point

\end{itemize}


\section{Public Entry Point}
\label{\detokenize{optima_algorithms:public-entry-point}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The top\sphinxhyphen{}level call takes a constrained problem, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ParameterPack\textless{}Series\textgreater{}}} initial point, and an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OptimaOptions}} value:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{using}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{namespace}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{subsp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{math}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n+nn}{optim}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{ConstrainedProblem}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{problem}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{ParameterPack}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{Series}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{OptimaOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{algorithm}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{OptimaAlgorithm}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{SequentialQP}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{optima}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{problem}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{x0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\section{Problem Model}
\label{\detokenize{optima_algorithms:problem-model}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Optima}} works with:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a scalar objective

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nonlinear equality constraints

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
nonlinear inequality constraints

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
linear equality constraints

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
linear inequality constraints

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
lower and upper bounds

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The public parameter surface is always \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ParameterPack\textless{}Series\textgreater{}}}. Derivatives come from either:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
autodiff callbacks over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ParameterPack\textless{}Trace\textgreater{}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
user\sphinxhyphen{}supplied analytic callbacks

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Autodiff/analytic are the derivative paths in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Optima}}.


\section{Shared Runtime Contract}
\label{\detokenize{optima_algorithms:shared-runtime-contract}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All current backends reuse the same evaluation layer and diagnostics:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
callback validation and shape checks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
non\sphinxhyphen{}finite evaluation detection

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
best\sphinxhyphen{}feasible tracking

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
multiplier reporting

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
progress hooks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stall classification

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
scaling and normalization

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
dense and iterative linear\sphinxhyphen{}system policies

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OptimaAlgorithm}} currently exposes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MeritMethod}} (baseline penalty\sphinxhyphen{}method backend)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SequentialQP}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WorkingSet}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{InternalProtocol}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The primary MATLAB\sphinxhyphen{}inspired constrained NLP backends are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SequentialQP}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{InternalProtocol}}.
This document focuses on those two:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Sequential QP}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{Internal Protocol}}}}}

\end{itemize}

\section{Progress Hooks}
\label{\detokenize{optima_algorithms:progress-hooks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each backend option block accepts a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{progress\_hook}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sequential\PYGZus{}qp}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{progress\PYGZus{}hook}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{OptimaProgressSnapshot}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{s}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The snapshot includes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stage}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{algorithm}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{params}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{evaluation}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{iteration}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{function\_evaluations}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step\_size}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{backend\_parameter}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stationarity}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{complementarity}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{krylov\_iterations}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{message}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stall\_category}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stall\_measure}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Returning \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} requests an orderly stop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reports::iter(std::ostream\&, precision)}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reports::iteration\_only\_trace(...)}}
are convenience factories for per\sphinxhyphen{}iteration output.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a MATLAB \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OutputFcn}}\sphinxhyphen{}style intercept, use a custom hook and return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}
when you want to stop before the next iteration.


\section{Internal Protocol Presets}
\label{\detokenize{optima_algorithms:internal-protocol-presets}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both presets below use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OptimaAlgorithm::InternalProtocol}}; the robust preset
just allocates more recovery budget and explicit solver defaults:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{presets::internal\_protocol()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{presets::robust\_internal\_protocol()}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Key robust deltas:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_iterations}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{160}} (vs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{100}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_restoration\_iterations}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_restoration\_line\_search\_iterations}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{enable\_restoration}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{enable\_feasibility\_phase}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hessian\_approximation}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bfgs}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{linear\_system\_solver}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Auto}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{system\_structure}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Auto}}

\end{itemize}


\section{Stall Taxonomy}
\label{\detokenize{optima_algorithms:stall-taxonomy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Optima}} surfaces structured failure modes instead of only generic stop messages:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{none}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{user\sphinxhyphen{}stop}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid\sphinxhyphen{}callback\sphinxhyphen{}contract}}

\chapter{Optima Sequential QP}
\label{\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp:optima-sequential-qp}}\label{\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SequentialQP}} is the dense constrained nonlinear\sphinxhyphen{}programming backend for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{optima(...)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is designed for derivative\sphinxhyphen{}based constrained optimization over moderate parameter counts, with gradients and Jacobians coming from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlussQit}} autodiff or analytic callbacks.


\section{Mathematical Problem}
\label{\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp:mathematical-problem}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The backend targets nonlinear programs of the form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
\min_x \quad & f(x) \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & c_{\mathrm{eq}}(x) = 0, \\
& c_{\mathrm{ineq}}(x) \le 0, \\
& A_{\mathrm{eq}} x = b_{\mathrm{eq}}, \\
& A_{\mathrm{ineq}} x \le b_{\mathrm{ineq}}, \\
& \ell \le x \le u.
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
At a candidate solution, the first\sphinxhyphen{}order KKT conditions are expressed in terms of the Lagrangian
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathcal{L}(x,\lambda,\nu)=
f(x)
 + \lambda_{\mathrm{eq}}^\top c_{\mathrm{eq}}(x)
 + \lambda_{\mathrm{ineq}}^\top c_{\mathrm{ineq}}(x)
 + \nu_{\mathrm{eq}}^\top (A_{\mathrm{eq}}x-b_{\mathrm{eq}})
 + \nu_{\mathrm{ineq}}^\top (A_{\mathrm{ineq}}x-b_{\mathrm{ineq}}).\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SequentialQP}} tracks a practical KKT residual derived from the gradient of this Lagrangian together with active constraint residuals.


\section{Solver Shape}
\label{\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp:solver-shape}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The backend works by repeating this major loop:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
evaluate objective and constraints

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
linearize constraints at the current point

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
build a local quadratic model of the Lagrangian

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
solve a KKT\sphinxhyphen{}style subproblem

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
apply line search and bound\sphinxhyphen{}feasible step control

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
optionally run second\sphinxhyphen{}order correction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
optionally run restoration if the main step fails

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
update the Hessian model and multiplier estimate

\end{enumerate}


\section{Local Quadratic Subproblem}
\label{\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp:local-quadratic-subproblem}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
At iteration \$k\$, the solver forms a quadratic model around the current point \$x\_k\$:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
\min_p \quad &
\nabla f(x_k)^\top p + \tfrac12 p^\top B_k p \\
\text{s.t.} \quad &
c_{\mathrm{eq}}(x_k) + J_{\mathrm{eq}}(x_k) p = 0, \\
& c_{\mathrm{ineq}}(x_k) + J_{\mathrm{ineq}}(x_k) p \le 0,
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\$B\_k\$ is the current Hessian approximation to the Lagrangian

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\$J\_\{\textbackslash{}mathrm\{eq\}\}\$ and \$J\_\{\textbackslash{}mathrm\{ineq\}\}\$ are Jacobians assembled from autodiff or analytic callbacks

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The implementation solves the corresponding KKT system using the configured linear\sphinxhyphen{}system policy.


\section{Main State}
\label{\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp:main-state}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The internal SQP state tracks:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current evaluation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
iteration count

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
function evaluation count

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current step size

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current penalty parameter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
current merit value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
KKT residual

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
convergence flag

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
message

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
best\sphinxhyphen{}feasible snapshot

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hessian approximation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
multiplier estimate

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
variable scaling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
normalization statistics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Krylov iteration count

\end{itemize}

\section{Hessian Handling}
\label{\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp:hessian-handling}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Current SQP Hessian policies:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bfgs}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Identity}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Hessian model is applied to the Lagrangian approximation inside the QP step.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bfgs}} is active, the update is based on the standard secant pair
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}s_k = x_{k+1} - x_k,\qquad
y_k = \nabla \phi_{k+1} - \nabla \phi_k,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \$\textbackslash{}phi\$ is the merit\sphinxhyphen{}gradient model used by the solver. The update is skipped when curvature is too small, controlled by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bfgs\_curvature\_tolerance}}.


\section{Linear\sphinxhyphen{}System Policy}
\label{\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp:linear-system-policy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The backend supports a policy\sphinxhyphen{}driven solve path:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Auto}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Cholesky}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PivotedDirect}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Inverse}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PseudoInverse}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ConjugateGradient}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Auto}} routes based on dimension and structure hints. Small dense systems usually stay on direct solves. Larger or structured problems can route to Krylov iterations when configured.


\section{Step Acceptance}
\label{\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp:step-acceptance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SequentialQP}} uses a merit\sphinxhyphen{}based acceptance policy with additional constrained safeguards:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Armijo decrease on the merit model

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stricter handling when the iterate is still infeasible

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
second\sphinxhyphen{}order correction when linearized feasibility is too optimistic

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
boundary\sphinxhyphen{}limited capping

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
restoration fallback when the main step cannot improve the merit or feasibility model

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The main merit model is an exact\sphinxhyphen{}penalty style scalarization:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\Phi(x;\rho) = f(x) + \rho \, \|v(x)\|_1,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \$v(x)\$ denotes the stacked constraint residual used by the implementation. The penalty parameter \$\textbackslash{}rho\$ is adapted when feasibility reduction is lagging.


\section{Second\sphinxhyphen{}Order Correction}
\label{\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp:second-order-correction}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After a first QP step \$p\_k\$ is found, the solver can attempt a second\sphinxhyphen{}order correction when nonlinear residuals are not captured well by the first linearization. In practice this means re\sphinxhyphen{}solving with a corrected residual target instead of accepting a step that only looks feasible in the local linear model.


\section{Restoration}
\label{\detokenize{optima_sequential_qp:restoration}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the main SQP step fails repeatedly, the backend can switch to a restoration phase that prioritizes violation reduction. A successful restoration step resets the local Hessian model before returning to the main loop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The restoration target is conceptually
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\min_x \; \|v(x)\|,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
subject to the same bound handling logic, so that the solver can recover a usable feasible or near\sphinxhyphen{}feasible point before resuming the main SQP loop.

\chapter{Optima Internal Protocol}
\label{\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol:optima-internal-protocol}}\label{\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{InternalProtocol}} is the Pluss\sphinxhyphen{}native public label for the primal\sphinxhyphen{}dual barrier backend currently implemented under the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OptimaAlgorithm::InternalProtocol}} enum branch.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The intent is straightforward:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the algorithmic family is still internal\sphinxhyphen{}protocol

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the public product naming stays Pluss\sphinxhyphen{}native

\end{itemize}


\section{Mathematical Problem}
\label{\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol:mathematical-problem}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The backend targets the same constrained nonlinear program:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\begin{aligned}
\min_x \quad & f(x) \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & c_{\mathrm{eq}}(x) = 0, \\
& c_{\mathrm{ineq}}(x) \le 0, \\
& A_{\mathrm{eq}} x = b_{\mathrm{eq}}, \\
& A_{\mathrm{ineq}} x \le b_{\mathrm{ineq}}, \\
& \ell \le x \le u.
\end{aligned}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For inequality handling, the solver introduces slack variables
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}c_{\mathrm{ineq}}(x) + s = 0,\qquad s > 0,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
and dual variables \$z \textgreater{} 0\$ for the slack equations.


\section{Solver Shape}
\label{\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol:solver-shape}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This backend uses a primal\sphinxhyphen{}dual barrier formulation with:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
explicit inequality slacks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
explicit inequality duals

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
complementarity tracking

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
barrier reduction over outer progress

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
feasibility\sphinxhyphen{}phase fallback

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
restoration handling

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The major loop is:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
evaluate the objective and constraints

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
assemble the barrier or primal\sphinxhyphen{}dual stationarity model

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
form a Newton\sphinxhyphen{}like or quasi\sphinxhyphen{}Newton direction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cap the step to preserve interiority

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
apply line search

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
update slack, dual, barrier, and curvature state

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
switch to feasibility or restoration modes if the main step stalls

\end{enumerate}


\section{Primal\sphinxhyphen{}Dual System}
\label{\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol:primal-dual-system}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The implementation follows a primal\sphinxhyphen{}dual barrier structure built around:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\nabla_x \mathcal{L}(x,\lambda,z) = 0,\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}c_{\mathrm{eq}}(x)=0,
\qquad
c_{\mathrm{ineq}}(x)+s=0,\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}S z = \mu \mathbf{1},
\qquad
s>0,\; z>0,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\$S=\textbackslash{}operatorname\{diag\}(s)\$

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\$\textbackslash{}mu\$ is the barrier parameter

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The complementarity residual reported by the solver is derived from the mismatch in the relation \$Sz=\textbackslash{}mu \textbackslash{}mathbf\{1\}\$.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
message

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
best\sphinxhyphen{}feasible snapshot

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hessian model

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
variable scaling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
normalization statistics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Krylov iteration count

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
limited\sphinxhyphen{}memory history

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{Barrier Objective View}
\label{\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol:barrier-objective-view}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the primal\sphinxhyphen{}dual residual system, it is useful to read the method as minimizing a barrier model of the form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\phi_\mu(x,s) =
f(x)
- \mu \sum_i \log(s_i)
+ \tfrac12 \rho \, \|c_{\mathrm{eq}}(x)\|_2^2,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
subject to \$c\_\{\textbackslash{}mathrm\{ineq\}\}(x)+s=0\$. This is also the right mental model for interpreting:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{backend\_parameter}} as the current \$\textbackslash{}mu\$

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{complementarity}} as the centrality/complementarity error

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{constraint\_violation}} as primal infeasibility

\end{itemize}

\section{Hessian Modes}
\label{\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol:hessian-modes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Supported curvature policies:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bfgs}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Identity}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Lbfgs}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HessianVector}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HessianVector}} rely on autodiff\sphinxhyphen{}capable callbacks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Exact}}, the target object is the Hessian of the Lagrangian\sphinxhyphen{}like barrier model with respect to the primal variables. For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HessianVector}}, the solver applies matrix\sphinxhyphen{}free curvature products inside the iterative subproblem path.


\section{Linear\sphinxhyphen{}System Policy}
\label{\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol:linear-system-policy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Supported policies:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Auto}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Cholesky}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PivotedDirect}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Inverse}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PseudoInverse}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ConjugateGradient}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For larger structured systems, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ConjugateGradient}} is the main matrix\sphinxhyphen{}free path and feeds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{krylov\_iterations}} in the final output.


\section{Barrier and Complementarity Trace}
\label{\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol:barrier-and-complementarity-trace}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The most useful live fields are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{backend\_parameter}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{complementarity}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stationarity}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{constraint\_violation}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step\_size}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{krylov\_iterations}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Those reveal whether the backend is:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
making central progress

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
reducing barrier pressure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stalling in complementarity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stuck in feasibility or recovery

\end{itemize}


\section{Feasibility Phase and Recovery}
\label{\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol:feasibility-phase-and-recovery}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the main primal\sphinxhyphen{}dual loop stalls, the backend can switch into a feasibility\sphinxhyphen{}focused mode. The intent is analogous to minimizing a violation measure
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\min_x \; \|v(x)\|,\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
before returning to the main primal\sphinxhyphen{}dual trajectory.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The recovery path is separate from the feasibility phase:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
feasibility phase: reduce primal infeasibility

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
recovery phase: regain a usable interior step when the barrier step itself fails

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These show up in the output through:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stall\_category}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{detail\_message}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{best\_feasible\_available}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{returned\_best\_feasible}}

\end{itemize}

The final multiplier structure is split into:

\section{Example Trace}
\label{\detokenize{optima_internal_protocol:example-trace}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A typical progress line from an instrumented run looks like:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
iter=35 evals=189 objective=16.329592 viol=0.000000 stationarity=0.244045 backend=0.010000 step=0.062500 stall=none
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Interpretation:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{value}}: current objective

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{viol}}: max constraint violation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stat}}: first\sphinxhyphen{}order stationarity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compl}}: complementarity residual

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{barrier}}: current barrier parameter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{step}}: accepted step fraction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{krylov}}: inner iterative solver work

\end{itemize}
